author: gaps
note: bars[0] is the reference (most recently closed) bar; index increases going back in time. Every fixture fixes bars[1] as the prior bar [100.0,101.0,99.0,100.5,4000] (high=101.0, low=99.0, range=2.0). Gap predicates compare open[0] strictly against high[1]/low[1]; exhaustion variants add r0 < 0.5*range[1] = r0 < 1.0. Only bars 0 and 1 (and range[1]) are read, so the index-2 filler is inert.

fixtures.rationale: A gap up means the session opens above the entire prior bar: open 102.0 is above the prior high 101.0, so price jumped with no overlap. This is the defining shape of a bullish gap.
Open 100.5 sits inside the prior bar's 99.0-101.0 range, so the market opened where yesterday already traded. No gap exists: continuous trading, not a jump.
Open 98.0 is below the prior low 99.0: this is a gap in the opposite direction (down), which is emphatically not a gap up and must not be reported as one.
Open 101.5 is above the prior high 101.0 by 0.5, clearly inside the gap-up region (over the strict open>high[1] threshold). Bracketed from above the threshold.
Open 100.8 is below the prior high 101.0 by 0.2, just under the open>high[1] threshold, so no gap. Paired with the above-case to bracket the threshold from below without float equality.

Open 101.0 exactly equals the prior high 101.0: touching, not gapping. Both are the same stored literal so equality is exact; the strict open>high[1] comparison excludes equality, proving strictness is intended (expected false, on the threshold).
A gap down means the session opens below the entire prior bar: open 98.0 is beneath the prior low 99.0, a downward jump with no overlap. The defining shape of a bearish gap.
Open 100.0 lies inside the prior 99.0-101.0 range: the market reopened where it already traded, so there is no downward gap, just continuous trading.
Open 102.0 is above the prior high 101.0: a gap in the opposite (up) direction, which is not a gap down and must not be reported as one.
Open 98.5 is below the prior low 99.0 by 0.5, clearly inside the gap-down region (under the strict open<low[1] threshold). Bracketed from below the threshold.
Open 99.2 is above the prior low 99.0 by 0.2, just over the open<low[1] threshold, so no gap down. Paired with the below-case to bracket the threshold from above without float equality.

Open 99.0 exactly equals the prior low 99.0: touching, not gapping. Same stored literal so equality is exact; the strict open<low[1] comparison excludes equality, proving strictness is intended (expected false, on the threshold).
Gap and go up: opens 102.0 above the prior high 101.0 (the gap) and then closes 103.0 above its open 102.0 (the go). Buyers held the gap and pushed further; the pattern's two halves are both present.
Attacks the gap clause: the bar is bullish (close 101.2 > open 100.5) but opens 100.5 inside the prior range, so there is no gap to run from. A rally without a gap is not gap-and-go.

Attacks the continuation clause: it gaps up (open 102.0 > prior high 101.0) but then closes 101.0 below its open 102.0. The gap was sold, the opposite of 'go' - this is failed follow-through, not gap-and-go.

Attacks the continuation clause at its edge: it gaps up but closes 102.0 exactly at its open 102.0. A flat bar has no directional 'go'; IsBull requires close strictly above open, so this is not gap-and-go.

Open 101.3 is above the prior high 101.0 by 0.3 (over the gap threshold) and the bar is bullish (101.8 > 101.3). Isolates the gap clause just inside the threshold with the continuation clause satisfied.

Open 100.8 is below the prior high 101.0 by 0.2 (under the gap threshold) though the bar is bullish. Changing only the open from the inside-case shows the gap clause is what rejects it, below the threshold.

Open 101.0 exactly equals the prior high 101.0: touching, not gapping, even though the bar is bullish. Exact literal equality; the strict open>high[1] gap clause excludes equality, so no gap-and-go (on the threshold).
Gap and go down: opens 98.0 below the prior low 99.0 (the gap) and then closes 97.0 below its open 98.0 (the go). Sellers held the gap and drove lower; both halves present.
Attacks the gap clause: the bar is bearish (close 99.3 < open 99.5) but opens 99.5 inside the prior range, so there is no downward gap to run from. A decline without a gap is not gap-and-go.
Attacks the continuation clause: it gaps down (open 98.0 < prior low 99.0) but then closes 99.0 above its open 98.0. The gap was bought back, the opposite of a bearish 'go'.

Attacks the continuation clause at its edge: it gaps down but closes 98.0 exactly at its open 98.0. A flat bar has no directional 'go'; IsBear requires close strictly below open, so this is not gap-and-go.
Open 98.7 is below the prior low 99.0 by 0.3 (under the gap threshold) and the bar is bearish (98.2 < 98.7). Isolates the gap clause just inside the threshold with continuation satisfied.
Open 99.2 is above the prior low 99.0 by 0.2 (over the gap threshold) though the bar is bearish. Changing only the open from the inside-case shows the gap clause rejects it, above the threshold.

Open 99.0 exactly equals the prior low 99.0: touching, not gapping, even though the bar is bearish. Exact literal equality; the strict open<low[1] gap clause excludes equality, so no gap-and-go (on the threshold).

Exhaustion gap up: opens 101.5 above the prior high 101.0 (gap), then reverses to close 101.2 below its open (bearish), on a narrow range of 0.7 that is well under half the prior range 2.0 (0.5*2.0=1.0). The gap stalled and turned - all three halves present.
Attacks the gap clause: bar is bearish and narrow (range 0.7) but opens 100.5 inside the prior range - no gap up to exhaust. Without the initial gap there is nothing for exhaustion to describe.
Attacks the reversal clause: gaps up (open 101.5 > prior high 101.0) and range is narrow (0.6), but closes 101.8 above its open (bullish). A gap that follows through up is gap-and-go, not exhaustion.

Attacks the range-shrink clause: gaps up and closes bearish, but the range is 2.0 (high 103.0 - low 101.0), not the small/stalling bar the exhaustion condition r0 < 0.5*prior-range (1.0) requires. A wide reversal bar is a different animal.
Range 0.9 (101.9-101.0) is inside the r0 < 0.5*range[1] = 1.0 shrink threshold. Gap (101.5>101.0) and bearish close (101.2<101.5) hold, isolating the range clause just below the threshold.

Range 1.1 (102.2-101.1) is outside (above) the 1.0 shrink threshold. Only the range changed from the inside-case; gap and bearish close still hold, so the range clause is what rejects it, over the threshold.

Open 101.0 exactly equals the prior high 101.0: touching, not gapping, though bearish and narrow (range 0.5). Exact literal equality; the strict open>high[1] gap clause excludes equality, so no exhaustion gap (on the gap threshold).

Exhaustion gap down: opens 98.5 below the prior low 99.0 (gap), then reverses to close 98.6 above its open (bullish), on a narrow range of 0.7 well under half the prior range 2.0 (threshold 1.0). The gap stalled and turned up - all three halves present.
Attacks the gap clause: bar is bullish and narrow (range 0.6) but opens 99.5 inside the prior range - no gap down to exhaust. Without the initial gap there is nothing for exhaustion to describe.
Attacks the reversal clause: gaps down (open 98.5 < prior low 99.0) and range is narrow (0.7), but closes 98.2 below its open (bearish). A gap that follows through down is gap-and-go, not exhaustion.

Attacks the range-shrink clause: gaps down and closes bullish, but the range is 2.0 (high 99.0 - low 97.0), not the small/stalling bar the exhaustion condition r0 < 0.5*prior-range (1.0) requires. A wide reversal bar is a different animal.
Range 0.9 (98.9-98.0) is inside the r0 < 0.5*range[1] = 1.0 shrink threshold. Gap (98.5<99.0) and bullish close (98.6>98.5) hold, isolating the range clause just below the threshold.

Range 1.1 (99.0-97.9) is outside (above) the 1.0 shrink threshold. Only the range changed from the inside-case; gap and bullish close still hold, so the range clause is what rejects it, over the threshold.

Open 99.0 exactly equals the prior low 99.0: touching, not gapping, though bullish and narrow (range 0.6). Exact literal equality; the strict open<low[1] gap clause excludes equality, so no exhaustion gap (on the gap threshold).
